category_title: Students who sleep during the course and challenge teacher directives when woken
minimal_context: The student is participating in a vocational high school course in a classroom setting.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are in the middle of the course. Please look at the board and continue taking notes on the vocational training material.

STUDENT: (Lifts head from the desk after sleeping) Teacher, they want to wash their face. I mean, I want to wash my face.

TUTOR: No, I do not give permission for you to leave the room right now.

STUDENT: Why not? I was just sleeping and I need to wake up. Just let me go out for a minute.

TUTOR: You need to stay in your seat and focus on the lesson.

STUDENT: This is ridiculous! I'm just asking to wash my face and you're making a huge deal out of it in front of the whole classroom. Why are you always causing problems over nothing?

options.A: Repeatedly stress that any relapses into disengagement will be accommodated and their place in the vocational course held open.
options.B: Discuss the negative effects of misbehaviors from different perspectives while explaining the disciplinary and behavioral rules in the classroom and school.
options.C: Deliver a structured mindfulness program consisting of twelve hour-long sessions, generally twice-weekly, throughout the vocational course.
options.D: Provide a clear beginning and end for each task while the student is working on the vocational training material.
